Perfume rating 3.79 out of 5 with 3,662 votes

Euphoria Men by Calvin Klein is a Woody Aromatic fragrance for men. Euphoria Men was launched in 2006. Euphoria Men was created by Carlos Benaïm, Loc Dong and Jean-Marc Chaillan. Top notes are Ginger and Pepper; middle notes are Black Basil, Sage and Cedar; base notes are Amber, Suede, Brazilian Redwood and Patchouli.

shamus1 06/23/25 14:26

Euphoria is not a typical "fresh" fragrance. The suede and redwood together make it stand out from the rest, adding some dark smokiness to the usual freshness. Euphoria isn't sporty, but rather dry, spicy and woody. It's discreet and classy.

Don't worry about all the comments on poor performance. This was not meant to be a powerhouse fragrance. Just do what I do: spray it all over your chest and inner arms (I use like 10 sprays), then put on a shirt. That way, both your skin and the fabric will have the scent. Although it never projects far, I can smell it as a skin scent for a good 8 hours. What more do you want? This is a wonderful fragrance!

Starbar 03/17/25 13:01

I used to wear this juice early 2000's. Seem to remember a great opening, then gone before the dry down. A bit like the girl who bought it for me😂.

Anyway, about a year and a half ago I had a voucher from some insurance scheme and used it on this stuff. It was the first time I'd acquired any cologne in years and was the kick-start of a new interest, hobby, obsession, curse! Call it what you will.

So, the first spray after all those years, and, I could barely smell anything. And what I could smell was like the water you boil vegetables in but weaker. Gone after half an hour max, thankfully. Well, I couldn't take it back and Glade does a better bathroom spray so I put it in the top of the wardrobe on its own, (it's a long way from being on its own now) .

Yesterday, I had to pop into town, so pre shower I opened up the wardrobe and started cruising the bottles for the frag of the day. Don't know why, maybe the hangover from Paddies day, nostalgia, don't know. Sprayed it on my hand, two half spritzes, and fuck me! What a difference. Instantly, we'll pretty much I got a green, herbal, woody quite fresh blast of a well blended English forest in spring after a shower when the sun comes out. Only way I can describe it really. Very pleasantly surprised.

Post shower, 6 half sprays, town, back home, could still smell it on me. Altogether about 5/6 hours. Not really changed much, quite linear, but still there and really nice and uplifting.

So, if you have the patience and can Pick it up cheap(it's cheap anyway) , get it, spray a few ml's and put it away for a year or two. You will be happy you did.

I enjoy this fragrance a lot. I first bought it in 2006. For various reasons (life), I went from 2010 - 2019 not wearing cologne at all. But I do like it very much and there's a time and place for cologne that quietly whispers in the background. I can smell it easily when I wear it, but the projection and longevity are short for a designer.

mkpunk 03/01/22 21:45

Calvin Klein Euphoria Men was one of my first fragrances that I got. I think I had 10 or so at that point. I smelt it on a card first walking through a Macy's before going into Sears and picking it up. This was roughly six years ago. It is a bit different than most fragrances. Euphoria Men is very woody and very aromatic. It is not citric at all and instead opens with a ginger and pepper heavy open. That said, the pepper is NOT Sauvage or Villain like, and a little more subdue, thank God. Euphoria then goes into a cedar heavy mid. The base is a bit ambery and redwoody too. I previously said that note wise, this doesn't work for me, but I now realize that was me thinking it earlier in my journey.

Euphoria Men I feel is a Calvin Klein take on Fierce. Now it isn't one to one by any means at all. Fierce has fir up top and musk in the base that Euphoria does not have. That said, both have a similar feel and do something similar. Both become a sexy second skin. Dior Homme 2020 also is similar-ish to Euphoria Men, but has a Dior sprayer and is a hot rod engine put inside of a normal mid-level sedan. Without trying and enjoying Euphoria Men, I would get to try two of my favorite fragrances, Dior Homme and Montblanc Legend Eau de Parfum.

Euphoria Men's problem is performance. A common issue with Calvin Klein is performance. Euphoria Men has rather low sillage. At the time Euphoria Men launched, Fierce was a hot rod engine itself. Euphoria Men also doesn't last. It lasts about four hours on my skin.

Euphoria Men I think works day or night from spring to fall. I cannot say winter due to the performance issues. I can see Euphoria Men working in a work setting, casual and yes, dates. It is a perfect close quarters scent. That said, if you want a more club ready version, get Montblanc Legend Eau de Parfum.

Overall I think I have to rate Calvin Klein Euphoria Men an even 7 out of 10. Before I found Dior Homme and Montblanc Legend Eau de Parfum, I would be asking for a Euphoria Men that is stronger. Gold takes the DNA in a sweeter direction and that is the only Euphoria flanker I've gotten my nose on.

misforwhat 12/11/19 13:24

This was given as a gift to me one year and I rarely use it--as others have said it isn't because I dislike the scent (I like it) I just have better options for almost any occasion.

It opens with strong ginger and pepper, and I enjoy both. While I wouldn't call it "euphoria" I would say there is a warm, uplifting sensation brought on by the initial shock of the pepper and the intensity of the ginger.

The sage and cedar come through nicely to create an herbal wooden aroma that reminds me of fine incense. It is very warm and earthy, but not too spicy after it dries. It is masculine but could probably be marketed as unisex. This isn't a bad thing, it is just more neutral than other CK men's fragrance (Shock, Obsession Night, ect.). Slightly synthetic as it dries, but not as bad as ambroxan-based fragrances that I use.

The problem, as others have noted, is that this spray has next-to-no longevity or projection. This is a strict blend-into-the-background aroma. It would be a good scent for the home or office if it lasted longer. After two or three hours it is pretty much gone. Some of it lingers directly on the skin for awhile longer, but it won't get you past lunch.

There are a few times one might want to reach for this--perhaps if you have a shower before bed and want to put something on while you wind down. After the pepper and ginger dry off the sage and cedar are very relaxing, and it expires quickly so you don't smell it as you sleep. It is also useful for formal occasions where you want to smell good for a few hours but not try and get attention (an interview, maybe a funeral).

Overall: Not recommended unless you got it as a gift, and then only if you only need it to work for the length of a feature-length film. But still a nice, fresh scent.

What I don't particularly like about it is the complete lack of focus, depth, and refinement, and offensively generic nature of the scent after the opening dies down. It’s synthetic AF, and truly smells just like a department store perfume counter. It's very easy to smell it and think "oh, nice scent!" but you would be hard pressed to differentiate this fragrance from a TON of other male frags. Overall, a good smelling, safe scent, but it will not blow you away, it truly is like a glorified body spray:generally pleasant, but insanely shallow, boring, it doesn’t even pretend to try to be anything new and exciting with depth . Longevity is not bad, better than Eternity, but again it's so damn boring after the opening, so you might want to top it off after an hour or two. Still, overall, it's (barely) a like from me, and you could do MUCH worse for a first scent, for a young man, etc.

5/10

Hell yeah I wear CK's Euphoria for men. It's one of those fragrances that feel like they made a mistake because it ought to be for WOMEN lol The same goes for CK's more popular and famous classic Eternity which is a floral fragrance. This one is not as floral but it's very sweet and spicy. Totally unisex. Ginger and pepper are notes that I've experienced and enjoyed in women's fragrances as well as amber, patchouli, suede and the woodsy note of Brazilian rose wood. All the notes in this fragrance create a soft, delicate, powdery and spicy aroma that makes you giddy with pleasure. Here are the notes Fragrantica lists

Top notes: ginger and pepper
Middle nots: basil, sage and cedar
Base notes: amber, patchouli, brazilian redwood and suede.

The way this fragrance starts is divine. It's not harsh, no aldehydes, no fruits, no citrus, nothing but delicious sweet ginger and pepper spices. It's such a shame the top notes disappear quickly. The heart is full of sage and basil, it's minty and green. The dry down is woodsy but it's also got amber and a very subdued patchouli. It's bigger on suede to my skin. This is a great fragrance but it's light and doesn't last as long as I would like it to. There is something like musk but it's probably the suede, it's the kind of musk I like because it's not too heavy. I like this spicy amber men's fragrance. It's innocent and boyish and reminds me of the way guys smelled when they were first trying out cologne in middle school to impress girls at dances. Now I don't mean that this is a juvenile and cheap scent. It can feel that way sometimes but the aromatic basil and patchouli give it that true grown up fragrance type of smell. It's not for everyone. I have a guy friend who could never wear this because the moment I say "this is unisex" he gets turned off by it. But try it if you're a guy or a girl that likes sweet and spicy ginger amber fragrances.

Pros:

- Sweet soft scent
- Inoffensive
- Has a calm seducitve scent to it
- Very nice peppery blend
- Not overpowered by wood notes
- Basic and simple notes that are constant
- Works well for the office or dinner out
- Works well for a younger age group

Cons:

- Sillage is extremly poor, only you will enjoy it
- Longevity is extremely poor
- 30 Minutes to climb through notes then will fade even faster until 60 minutes when its gone (all this on a good day)
- Constant reapplication will drain bottle and become expensive quickly
- Doesn't work well on a more mature type

Calvin Klein always seems to have a longevity and sillage problem. It never lasts as long or projects as far as you may want. When it comes to Euphoria, it is no better. It doesn't last long enough to reach "Euphoria". The general scenario is: You are getting ready for a date, put some CKE on trying to smell good (Peak for 5-10 mintues), you get in the car/on the bus (Drydown for 15-20 minutes), you get the restuarant and CKE is already ready to pack it in for the night as at about 30 minutes it nosedives to nothing.

It smells great, don't get me wrong, but that really doesn't do a whole lot when nobody can enjoy it within the 30 mintue time frame. Also they need to be right intimately close to you to actually detect it. I want to say that I love it, but I can't because it is a letdown. I do not recommend buying this on the basis of longevity and sillage alone.

peferrarine 07/04/14 11:21

An amazing scent. Yes, is not great on the sillage/projection department, but that doesn't mean the scent is not good.

Is sexy enough so it can be used in a dinner for two, or at a date, but not in your face, so i can see it being used in business meetings and at the office.

In my skin, is a light spicy, slightly herbal. The woody notes keeps it dry, and the amber note keeps it from being 'sport' fresh.
I find it very sensual. Is manly and modern. Clean but sophisticated. The color suits it well.

Is young, but not boyish. Is for that confident man who doesn't need his fragrance to enter a room before himself. You can smell him when you hold him, and you'll be very pleased by it.

Is not unique (you'll probably get that 'i know this one' feeling), but is not that common either.
The notes are VERY well blended, so there is no sharp notes.

It stays close to my skin, and when the weather is a little warmer you can get whiffs of it with the breeze. Unfortunately it disappears from my skin after a couple hours (that's why i think is more appropriate for intimate dinners, dates or business situations).

The lack of projection and longevity may be a bummer, but that should not keep you from trying this one. If you like it, you can find a place to use it.

PS: It shares some similarities with the Intense version. Actually, the Intense version should be the original EDT, and this one could be sold as an Euphoria L'Eau, or a summer version (due to the lightness)

UPDATE: i like to wear it at the gym, cause is not offensive, and keeps me fresh and slightly perfumed for the entire work-out session.

Calvin Klein Euphoria is a bit ubiquitous and easy to obtain at a discounted price (since it has been around awhile), but I am more than willing to recommend it. I call it my “spa” fragrance. I always pack a bottle of this in my bag when heading off to relax and rejuvenate because it just seems to produce those effects for me. In fact, if I am just feeling tired or distracted a spray or two of CKE returns me to composure.

CKE is not an attention grabber. It is a minimalist wood-leather composition with a subtle oriental arc meant to induce a sense of well-being and compliment the Calvin Klein fashion aesthetic. I like everything about this elixir: the ginger-pepper opening is assuaged by black basil and sage (members of the mint family) and figure into the liberation of the amber, cedar, and Brazilian redwood in a most pleasing way. After awhile, I am left with a Zen-like aura of mild woody suede and patchouli. The last phase stays close to my skin a long time and is very calming.

Some folks insist Calvin Klein sold out and, yes, there are esoteric fragrances which will take you to a higher place, but I have obtained a lot of pleasure from the very accessible CKE and his intense brother. (That’s a story for another day!) If there are a few synthetic molecules in the room they don't seem to bother me.

In 2006, Calvin Klein decided to launch another of its fresh scents, with the main philosophy inspired by the man and freedom to meet his dreams. So was born Euphoria Men, by the hands of Carlos Benaim and Loc Dong.

Euphoria Men usually pleases easily but also disappoints many users in terms of durability. As the lasting factor is something very personal, because it also depends on skin chemistry, I will just describe the fragrance and let in your hands the willingness to try it or not.

Euphoria Men brings, in its output, an exotic cocktail of ginger, pepper, and lemon, along with an innovative accord of rain. In the heart, cedar, basil, and sage. Finally, a woody base of patchouli, suede, sequoia, and an amber touch. The fragrance is versatile and refreshing, with a fairly youthful, aromatic, and decent appeal.

The bottle brings metallic protection and has good ergonomics. Besides, it is worth remembering that this perfume won the People’s Choice for Men in the UK Fragrance Foundation Awards in 2007.

TheNewEra 10/05/15 18:14

Pros:

- Sweet soft scent
- Inoffensive
- Has a calm seducitve scent to it
- Very nice peppery blend
- Not overpowered by wood notes
- Basic and simple notes that are constant
- Works well for the office or dinner out
- Works well for a younger age group

Cons:

- Sillage is extremly poor, only you will enjoy it
- Longevity is extremely poor
- 30 Minutes to climb through notes then will fade even faster until 60 minutes when its gone (all this on a good day)
- Constant reapplication will drain bottle and become expensive quickly
- Doesn't work well on a more mature type

Calvin Klein always seems to have a longevity and sillage problem. It never lasts as long or projects as far as you may want. When it comes to Euphoria, it is no better. It doesn't last long enough to reach "Euphoria". The general scenario is: You are getting ready for a date, put some CKE on trying to smell good (Peak for 5-10 mintues), you get in the car/on the bus (Drydown for 15-20 minutes), you get the restuarant and CKE is already ready to pack it in for the night as at about 30 minutes it nosedives to nothing.

It smells great, don't get me wrong, but that really doesn't do a whole lot when nobody can enjoy it within the 30 mintue time frame. Also they need to be right intimately close to you to actually detect it. I want to say that I love it, but I can't because it is a letdown. I do not recommend buying this on the basis of longevity and sillage alone.
